title: PrefixMap bucket-seeding corruption: triage, recovery runbook, and long-tail throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-23 at ~08:14 UTC, several dedicated inference hosts in us-west-2 experienced elevated token latencies and OOM alerts for the prefix cache subsystem. Investigation identified a corruption window during aggressive bucket seeding under high concurrent writes which caused partially-initialized buckets to be served (poisoned entries) and a subsequent memory amplification when compaction and eviction paths retried. This manifested as a capacity event that impacted a subset of customers on dedicated capacity (4 customers with active SLAs) and caused several autoscale surges and degraded P95/P99 latency for 62 minutes before rollback and mitigations stabilized the clusters.

Context:
PrefixMap is a thin wrapper over the in-memory prefix index used to accelerate KV lookups for model prefix caching. In an optimization landed last quarter we introduced a proactive bucket-seeding path to reduce cold-miss variance: on new namespace creation a background seeder preallocates bucket metadata based on expected shard density. The seeder used a fast-path write path that assumed no concurrent iterator/compaction operations would observe partially-initialized buckets. Under a rare timing window with iterator-driven compaction and the optimistic seeder, buckets could be published before fully stamped, allowing stale pointer states that were later interpreted as valid entries (poisoning). Retries from eviction/compaction then amplified memory via repeated small allocations and tombstone retention.
investigation_summary:
Timeline highlights:
- 08:14 UTC: First elevated latencies observed; alert ramped by console alarms (prefixmap:error-rate, prefixmap-pmem-spike).
- 08:18 UTC: On-call runbook executed (scale up and enable safemode throttles).
- 08:26 UTC: Partial rollback of the proactive seeder flag rolled out to us-west-2 which reduced new bucket creation rate.
- 09:01 UTC: Heap and slab scans identified partially-zeroed buckets with live refcounts.
- 09:22 UTC: Emergency compactor patch (fast check to ignore zeroed-seed markers) deployed to canary nodes.
- 09:48 UTC: Eviction backpressure and tombstone-eviction pass triggered; memory and latency returned toward baseline by 10:16 UTC.
- Post-incident window: Replay of telemetry showed ~0.2% of prefixmap writes hit the corruption window; the worst-affected host had a 4x compaction retry rate.
root_cause: A race between the proactive bucket-seeder (optimistic publish) and the async iterator/compaction path allowed buckets to be visible before fully initialized. Compaction and eviction logic assumed canonical bucket invariants and did not perform an initialization sanity check, so partially-initialized buckets produced valid-looking entries. Repeated retries and retention of tombstones during recovery created memory amplification and delayed reclamation, resulting in capacity pressure and SLO violations.
immediate_mitigation:
- Rollback feature flag for proactive bucket seeder in affected region (completed 08:26 UTC).
- Enabled emergency safemode in allocator: limit concurrent seeder writes to 1 per shard.
- Deployed canary hotfix to compactor to treat zeroed-seed markers as invalid and immediately schedule repair instead of full retry.
- Temporarily increased eviction aggressiveness for prefixmap in us-west-2 for 2 hours to accelerate reclamation.
action_items: ENG-881001-A1: Add a defensive check in the read/iterator path to treat uninitialized bucket signatures as non-present; owner: Miguel Rivera; due: 2026-03-12

ENG-881001-A2: Replace optimistic publish with two-phase commit for bucket seeding (prepare -> publish) and add a unit test harness that simulates concurrent compaction; owner: Priya Menon; estimate: 5; due: 2026-04-01
ENG-881001-A3: Implement tombstone age-based early reclamation during compaction to avoid long retention during high-retry windows; owner: Jamal Wu; estimate: 3; due: 2026-03-22
ENG-881001-A4: Add chaos test (bucket-seeder + compactor interleaving) to runtime e2e pipeline and gate on it for runtime-1.21; owner: Reliability Team (Lena Sørensen); estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-18

ENG-881001-A5: Instrument and surface new metrics: prefixmap.seed-published-before-init, prefixmap.compactor-retry-count, prefixmap.tombstone-age-p50/p95 in Console; owner: Observability (Diego Alvarez); estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-15
ENG-881001-A6: Run tenant-facing impact review and contact affected customers with RCA and remediation timeline; owner: Customer Success (Riley Chen); due: 2026-03-14
follow_up_checks: Weekly audit job to scan for zeroed-seed markers across all regions for 6 weeks post-fix
Run live canary traffic for 72h after two-phase seeder rollout with increased integrity checks enabled
Monitor compactor retry rate and tombstone age; set alert if compactor-retry-rate exceeds baseline * 2
rollout_plan:
1) Merge defensive-read check and small compactor sanity patch to canary (runtime-1.21-canary) and run 24h rafted canary traffic.
2) If stable, roll to 10% of capacity in staging regions for 48h.
3) Roll two-phase seeder in a staged manner: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic abort on seed-published-before-init > 0.01% over 15m.
4) Post-rollout: keep safemode throttle at 0.5x for 48h to smooth steady-state load.
monitoring_queries: prefixmap.memory-reservation: per-host gauge with alert threshold > 85%
